purpose: Defines the callisto command-line surface a user or CI script sees: commands, global flags, output formats, exit codes, and the behavior of status, add, init, pre, snapshot, completions and schema, plus the release workflow init generates.
scope: Command surface and help, global flags, text and JSON output, colour, exit codes, status, add, init, generated workflows and callisto-action modes, pre, snapshot, completions, schema.
non_goals: Release planning, publishing and receipts behind `callisto release` and its hidden subcommands.
Version planning, cascade and changelog rules behind `callisto version`.
The callisto.toml schema beyond the keys init writes.
Managed release-PR decisions made by the hidden `release-pr` plumbing.

api_surface.name: add
api_surface.description: Writes one changeset to .changeset/<adjective>-<noun>-<verb>.md, from flags or, with no --package and a terminal stdin, from an interactive wizard.
error_conditions: No --package and stdin is not a terminal.
--package given without --summary, or with a blank summary.
A --package value without `:severity`, with a severity other than none, patch, minor or major, or naming a package not in the workspace.

api_surface.name: status
api_surface.description: Shows each package's current version and planned bump, the pending package count, and diagnostics.
error_conditions: With --check, any error-level diagnostic (after --strict escalation) exits 1.

api_surface.name: version
api_surface.description: Consumes pending changesets and applies the planned version bumps.
error_conditions: With --strict, no pending changesets exits 1 with an error diagnostic.

api_surface.name: pre
api_surface.signature: callisto pre enter <TAG> | callisto pre exit
api_surface.description: Enters or exits prerelease mode by writing .changeset/pre.json.
error_conditions: `pre enter` while already in prerelease mode.
`pre exit` after prerelease mode was already exited, or with no .changeset/pre.json.

api_surface.name: snapshot
api_surface.description: Sets every package's manifest version to 0.0.0-<TAG>-<short HEAD sha> without consuming changesets.

api_surface.name: init
api_surface.description: Detects the workspace, asks only for intent, previews the first release, then writes callisto.toml, .changeset/README.md and optionally .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml.
error_conditions: Not inside a Git repository, or no `origin` remote.
A package matches more than one tag convention, or more than one package matches `v{version}`.
stdin is not a terminal and --yes is absent; --yes without a required flag.
--workflow when a workflow file already exists or the workspace shape has no generated workflow.

api_surface.name: release
api_surface.description: Publishes every package whose current version is unreleased; with --dry-run prints the release plan only.
error_conditions: Any planning or publishing failure exits 1; `Nothing to release.` exits 0.

api_surface.name: completions
api_surface.description: Prints a shell completion script to stdout.
error_conditions: An unsupported shell name (usage error, exit 2).

api_surface.name: schema (hidden)
api_surface.description: Prints the JSON Schema for a report type (status by default; also version, snapshot, validate, init, changeset, pre, matrix, release-receipt).
error_conditions: An unknown --type exits 1 listing the supported types.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `callisto --help` lists eight commands (add, status, version, pre, snapshot, init, release, completions), each with a one-line description, plus the global options --format, --cwd, --dry-run, --help and --version.
`matrix`, `schema`, `compose-pr-body`, `release-pr`, and `release plan|inspect|artifact-manifest|execute` are absent from `--help` output but still parse and run when invoked.
`--format`, `--cwd` and `--dry-run` are accepted before or after any subcommand name; --format defaults to text and --cwd defaults to the current directory.
With --dry-run, add, init, pre, snapshot and version write nothing; text output marks the preview with `[DRY-RUN]`.

When stdout is a terminal and NO_COLOR is unset, `status` and `release --dry-run` render a box-drawing table with ANSI colour; when stdout is piped they print plain indented lines with no ANSI codes or box-drawing characters.
A non-empty NO_COLOR disables colour and tables even when CLICOLOR_FORCE or FORCE_COLOR is set; an empty NO_COLOR is ignored.
CLICOLOR_FORCE or FORCE_COLOR (any value) turns colour and tables on for piped stdout, and CLICOLOR=0 turns them off on a terminal.
Text output of status, add, init, pre, snapshot and release --dry-run never contains a schema version string such as `schema v1`.
With `--format json`, the status, add, init, pre and snapshot reports on stdout are single JSON objects with camelCase keys and a top-level `schemaVersion`.
When a command fails under `--format json`, stderr ends with a JSON object `{"schemaVersion", "error": {"code", "message", "help"}}` and the exit code is 1.
When a command fails under text format, stderr shows a diagnostic with an error code and a message, and the exit code is 1.

Argument parsing errors (unknown flag, missing required argument, invalid value) exit 2 with clap's usage message; every other failure exits 1 and every success exits 0, including --dry-run previews and `release` reporting `Nothing to release.`

`callisto status`, with or without a callisto.toml, prints one row per package with its name, current version and planned bump (or `none`), then `<N> package(s) pending`, then a `Diagnostics:` section when any exist.
A package with no changeset of its own that `callisto version` would bump through dependency cascade or a fixed or linked group shows that planned bump in status and counts toward the pending total.

`status --format json` reports `hasChangesets`, `pending` (count of packages with a planned bump), and per package `package`, `currentVersion`, `lastReleasedVersion`, `pendingSeverity` (omitted when no bump is planned), `changedSinceLastTag`, `releaseTrigger` and `pendingChangesets`.
`callisto status` without --check always exits 0; `status --check` exits 0 when no diagnostic is error-level, regardless of pending changesets, and exits 1 when any diagnostic is error-level.

A changeset naming an unknown, ambiguous or invalid package produces an error-level diagnostic naming the changeset file, so `status --check` exits 1; a changeset that fails to parse (empty, blank summary, malformed entry) makes `status` exit 1 with the parse error.
`status --strict` reports strict-escalatable warnings as errors, so `status --check --strict` exits 1 where `status --check` exits 0.

`callisto add --package <name>:<severity> --summary <text>` (--package repeatable, bare or qualified names such as `cargo/app`, severity none, patch, minor or major) writes `.changeset/<adjective>-<noun>-<verb>.md` with front matter mapping each package to its severity and the trimmed summary as body, prints `Added changeset: <path>`, and never prompts.
`add --format json` prints `{"schemaVersion", "command": "add", "path"}`; with --dry-run it prints `dryRun: true`, the path and the file content, and creates no file or directory.

`callisto add` with no --package and a terminal stdin runs a wizard asking, in order, which packages to include, which are major, which remaining are minor (the rest are patch), a non-empty summary unless --summary was given, and a final confirmation; declining the confirmation writes nothing and exits 0.
`callisto add` with no --package and a non-terminal stdin exits 1 with error `callisto::not_a_tty` whose help names `callisto add --package <name>:<severity>`.
`add --package` without --summary, or with a whitespace-only summary, exits 1 naming --summary and writes nothing.

A --package value missing `:severity`, with an unknown severity, or naming a package not in the workspace exits 1 with a message naming the bad value (and, for an unknown package, listing the known packages) and writes nothing.
Before any question, `callisto init` prints `Detected:` with the ecosystems, the origin remote URL, and each package's qualified id, version, last tag, and binary names for binary-producing packages.

Interactive init asks only: versioning (independent or fixed); whether to ship binaries as GitHub release assets, only when a package produces a binary; the product package, only when more than one does; the forge repository, pre-filled from origin; comma-separated target triples; whether to generate a workflow (default no); and whether to write callisto.toml (default yes).
A supplied flag (--versioning, --artifact-target, --product-package, --forge-repository, --workflow, --no-workflow) skips its question, and declining the final write question writes no file.

The written callisto.toml starts with `# callisto configuration` and contains only answered intent: a `[[fixed-group]]` named `all` listing every non-platform package for fixed versioning, a `[[package]]` `tag-template` for each package whose existing tags follow a non-default convention, and, when shipping binaries, `publish-to` with `github-release` on the product plus a `[release]` table with `product-package`, `forge-repository` and one `[[release.artifact]]` per target and binary.

Tag detection matches each package's tags against `{name}@{version}` (default, never written), `{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}` and `v{version}`, and writes the single matching non-default convention as that package's tag-template.
init exits 1 without writing when a package matches more than one tag convention (listing each with its tags) or when more than one package matches `v{version}`.

After the config, init prints the first-release preview that `callisto release --dry-run` would show under it, or `No commits yet: commit, then run \`callisto release --dry-run\` to preview the first release.` when HEAD has no commit.
A successful init writes callisto.toml and creates .changeset/README.md only when it does not already exist.
init exits 1 without writing when callisto.toml already exists, when the directory is not inside a Git repository, or when no `origin` remote is configured, each with a help line naming the fix.

With a non-terminal stdin and no --yes, init exits 1 with `callisto::init_requires_yes` naming --yes and every other missing flag; with --yes it exits 1 with `callisto::init_missing_flags` naming each missing flag: --versioning always, --forge-repository when --artifact-target is given, and --product-package when --artifact-target is given and more than one package produces a binary.

With --yes, omitting --artifact-target writes no `[release]` table; --artifact-target is repeatable and comma-separated, and --workflow with --no-workflow exits 1 with `callisto::init_workflow_flags_conflict` before writing.

init exits 1 without writing for an empty or repeated target triple, --artifact-target when no package produces a binary, a --product-package that is absent or not binary-producing, or, when binaries ship, a --forge-repository that is not `owner/repo` or differs from origin's GitHub repository.

`init --format json` writes the human-readable detection, config and preview to stderr and a report `{schemaVersion, initialized, configPath, config}` (plus `diagnostics` when any) to stdout; with --dry-run `initialized` is false and no file is written.

A workflow is written to .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml only when --workflow is given or the interactive workflow question is answered yes; after writing, init prints that merging to the default branch publishes and advises requiring pull requests and reviews on it.
init never overwrites an existing .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml: when a workflow is requested and the file exists, init exits 1 before writing any file.

Without artifact slots or platform packages, the generated workflow triggers on push to the default branch (from origin/HEAD, else `main`) and has two jobs: `version-pr` running callisto-action with `mode: version-pr`, and `release` running it with `mode: release` and a token secret per detected ecosystem (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN with NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE, PYPI_TOKEN) plus GH_TOKEN.

When binaries ship as artifact slots or the workspace has napi platform packages, the generated workflow has `version-pr`, `plan` (runs `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` when the pushed commit adds or modifies .callisto/release-decision.json), `build` (a matrix from napi targets and artifact slots), and `execute` (runs `callisto release artifact-manifest` and `callisto release execute`) jobs.
Every callisto-action reference in a generated workflow is pinned to the commit SHA of the `callisto@<cli version>` tag, and init exits 1 when that tag cannot be resolved.

For a workspace with maturin platform targets, or platform packages without napi targets, init prints `Skipping GitHub Actions workflow generation: <reason>.`, records a warning diagnostic in the JSON report, and exits 1 instead when --workflow was given.

callisto-action accepts `mode: version-pr` (default; creates or updates the release PR and outputs `hasChangesets`) and `mode: release` (runs `callisto --format json release` and outputs `published` and `publishedPackages`); any other mode fails the step.
`callisto pre enter <tag>` writes .changeset/pre.json with mode `pre`, the tag and each package's initial version; `callisto pre exit` sets its mode to `exit`.
`pre enter` while in prerelease mode, and `pre exit` after prerelease mode was already exited, exit 1 naming the next step; `pre exit` with no .changeset/pre.json exits 1.
`callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` sets every package's manifest version to `0.0.0-<tag>-<short HEAD sha>`, prints each `from → to`, and leaves changesets in place.
`callisto completions <shell>` prints a completion script for bash, elvish, fish, powershell or zsh and exits 0.
`callisto schema` prints the StatusReport JSON Schema; `--type` selects another report type, and an unknown type exits 1 listing the supported types.
